title: ID0388605-DC/Si-D/PL[170001476] - Energy costs
description:
Reported behaviour/issue: Total energy of charger
Root cause:
Question for customer
Solution:
For the accuracy of the measurements, the Converter is declared by Huawei to have a “<0.5%” accuracy for voltage and <1% current:
So that would mean that in the worst case scenarios (-1% and -0.5% & +1% and +0.5%):
1- P=V*I = P=(100+0.5)*(100+0.5) = 10.1kW
2- 99.5*99.5 = 9.9kW
Instead of 100*100=10kW
The accuracy is a range so I cannot say if the customer will always favor CPO or customer.
For the power converter reactive control I can only say that it must be with the new Huawei converters:
R100040G4 comes with VPFC functionality (variable power factor correction). the first firmware of this converter enables the control of the reactive power consumption/ generation between -13kvar and +13kvar
After this information there is no specification on how it works.
I would suggest reaching out to the Regional Management colleague (SI E RM) so that he can arrange these answers for you.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0388605-DC/Si-D/PL[170001476] - Energy costs CRM:00315002018
additional_info.body:
Hello Francisco!
Thank you for your support in the last topics! Hope all is well with you!
Brief description of the situation:
According to the Orlen customer, the Sicharge D charger consumes 440 kWh in 1 month. This was calculated based on the electricity bill and transactions from the backend system.
The charger is equipped with a reactive power compensator. The energy consumed for captive use appears to be similar, but we need to confirm a few things.
In keeping with our conversation, I'm throwing in a few questions:
- measurement is implemented through SECC and power modules - what kind of measurement accuracy do we have here? What is the difference between the measured value and the real value? Do we have any graphs here, tests in this area?
- does the charger with such a solution:
- favors the EV user - that is, provides more energy to the customer than it indicates in MeterValues?
- favors the CPO - that is, it delivers less energy to the EV user than it indicates in MeterValues?
We are able to install DC meters, do the upgrade. The question is, what will it give us and what conclusions will we get in relation to the above questions?
Will the DC meters confirm that the station is supplying more energy than it indicated in the MeterValues and thus confirm that it was not the one using so much energy in the Standby state?
Here I'll immediately whine about the v6.0 software, which is the one that is supposed to turn off the power modules in the Standby state.
Can I ask you to give a technical overview of this solution?
1. will the station reduce reactive power in this way, if so, in what physical way? Will it disconnect: power modules, filter or maybe 3VA?
2. what if the station will use 1 power group, and 3 will not be used? Will reactive power then be generated from the 3 power groups?
3. will v6.0 limit active power? For example, by blanking the screen? Some kind of optimization?
I ask because we need to present the customer with an idea for the future on how we will limit the active power in standby. This is a real cost to the customer that may divert them from buying our stations.
We have in prospect several hundred chargers over a period of five years, not only in Poland.
If we have any documentation, please attach it. The case is very important.
With best regards,
Szymon Brodowicz
